gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold: patient presents with diarrhoea. Generated CC includes 3 days of diarrhea with vomiting and feverish symptoms; no separate simple statement that the presenting complaint is diarrhoea alone. The 3‑day duration contradicts the gold chief complaint which does not include duration, so it cannot be considered a clean cover.
Gold: 3‑day history of diarrhoea. Gen hpi-001: 'Symptoms began approximately 3 days ago.' This matches the duration of the illness.

Gold: stools are watery. Gen mentions watery/very loose diarrhea (hpi-002) but there is no gold text supporting that change from watery to very loose; gold specifies watery only. Therefore the exact gold fact is not cleanly restated.
Gold: sense of urgency with bowel movements. No generated fact explicitly mentions urgency to defecate.
Gold: no blood in stool. Gen hpi-008: 'no blood in the stool or urine.' This includes the gold element (no blood in stool).

Gold: periumbilical abdominal cramps that come in waves. Gen hpi-009: intermittent, crampy abdominal pain around the umbilicus, but does not specify 'comes in waves'; it rephrases character but not fully. So the exact gold characterization (comes in waves) is not captured.
Gold: cramps worse when she needs to open bowels. No generated fact links worsening pain to the need to open bowels.

Gold: four bowel movements by midday today. Gen hpi-003: 'at least four times today' without time qualifier (by midday). The midday qualifier is missing, and 'at least four' adds a different nuance, so the gold fact is not exactly captured.
Gold: patient has been vomiting. Gen hpi-005: 'The patient is vomiting...' clearly covers this.
Gold: feels not keeping fluids down. Gen hpi-005: 'unable to keep fluids down.' This restates the same idea.
Gold: still passing urine, last void 1 hour ago. Gen hpi-007: last passed urine about 1 hour ago. Also pf-003 echoes this. This covers the gold fact.

Gold: normal bowel habit once per day. Gen hpi-010: 'had a normal bowel habit prior to this illness'—while not specifying once per day, it captures the core fact that bowel habit was normal. Partial loss of detail but conceptually covered.
Gold: no foreign travel. Gen hpi-011: 'no recent travel.' This covers the absence of travel.
Gold: brother had similar symptoms. Gen hpi-012 and sh-008 both state the brother has similar symptoms; household transmission comment is additional.
Gold: mother also had similar symptoms and patient was in contact with her. No generated fact mentions the mother’s symptoms or this contact.

Gold: has been taking ORT regularly but has difficulty keeping it down. Gen mentions ORS in the plan but not that she had already been taking it regularly or having difficulty keeping it down in that historical sense.
Gold: patient reports no rash. Gen ros-001: ROS notable for absence of rash. Direct match.

Gold: feels hot but hasn't checked temperature. Gen hpi-004 says feels feverish/very hot to touch, but does not state that temperature has not been checked; it changes the characterization (adds 'very hot to touch'). Thus the precise gold nuance (no measured temp) is not captured.
Gold: LMP 2 weeks ago. Gen sh-005: last menstrual period ~2 weeks ago. This matches.

Gold: does not have regular sexual intercourse. Gen sh-007: 'not sexually active'—this is stronger and not equivalent to 'no regular SI.' Therefore the gold nuance (may have infrequent SI) is not correctly represented.
Gold: not using contraception. Gen sh-006: 'not on contraception.' Directly covers this.
Gold: has been at work till today; now working from home. No generated fact discusses work status around the illness (only occupation).
Gold: no significant past medical history. Gen pmh-001 matches this.

Gold: patient takes vitamins (non-specific). Gen med-001: vitamin D daily (specific). Since gold doesn’t specify vitamin D, the exact gold statement 'vitamins' is not matched; gen adds unsubstantiated specificity.
Gold: lives with brother and mother. Gen sh-001 states the same.
Gold: non-smoker. Gen sh-003: 'non-smoker.' Match.
Gold: drinks approximately one pint of alcohol per week. Gen sh-004: 'drinks alcohol socially'—this is vague and does not preserve the quantified amount of one pint/week.
Gold: works as graphic designer. Gen sh-002: graphic designer. Covered.
Gold FH: brother with similar GI symptoms. Gen hpi-012 and sh-008 state this; adequately covered.
Gold FH: mother also experienced similar GI symptoms. No generated fact mentions the mother’s symptoms.

Gold assessment: gastroenteritis, likely viral or food-related ('?Viral/?food poisoning'). Gen asm-001: acute infectious gastroenteritis likely viral with possible bacterial etiology; mentions bacterial but not food poisoning. This changes the differential etiology and does not include the 'food poisoning' angle, so the gold impression is not faithfully captured.

Gold: if fever persists, a stool culture will be sent to exclude bacterial origin. Gen plan-006: consider stool culture if symptoms persist or worsen to evaluate for bacterial infection. This is similar but not tied specifically to fever persistence as in the gold; thus the gold condition is not exactly captured.

Gold: continue taking small sips of ORT constantly. Gen plan-001: continue ORS with small, frequent sips and avoid overfilling stomach. The hydration instruction is captured; 'constantly' vs 'frequent' is close enough conceptually.
Gold: avoid fruits, vegetables, and milk for now. Gen plan-002: avoid fruit/veg and milk initially. This matches.

Gold: urgent appointment to assess hydration status. Gen plan-003 and fu-001: urgent clinic appointment for hydration assessment and stool sample. Because gold does NOT state stool sampling at that visit, and gen adds that as part of the same arranged appointment, the gold fact (urgent appointment solely to assess hydration status) is not exactly preserved.

Gold: if worse, abdominal pain or unwell, contact clinic to arrange urgent A&E assessment. Gen safety-net (plan-007, plan-010) refers to worsening symptoms/dehydration seeking urgent care but does not explicitly route via contacting the clinic to arrange urgent A&E; the pathway is different. So this specific follow-up instruction is not captured.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Generated CC: '3 days of diarrhea with vomiting and feverish symptoms.' Gold CC is only 'Diarrhoea' with no mention of duration, vomiting, or fever in the chief complaint. Duration belongs in HPI in gold, not CC, and adding vomiting/fever to the chief complaint misrepresents that section. Thus it conflicts with the documented chief complaint.

Gen: 'Diarrhea started watery and is now very loose.' Gold only states 'Watery stools' and does not document a change over time or 'very loose.' This evolution is not in gold and asserts a new temporal change, conflicting with the static description.

Gen: diarrhea at least 4 times today. Gold: '4 x by midday.' Gen omits 'by midday' and uses '≥4', which alters timing and certainty. It's not directly supported; it's a modified, broadened statement, so treated as an addition.

Gen: feels feverish and very hot to touch. Gold: 'Feels hot but hasn't checked temperature.' No mention of being 'very hot to touch' or 'feverish' as a clinical impression, so these are added qualifiers.
Gen: last vomiting episode ~2 hours ago after breakfast. Gold only states 'Vomiting' with difficulty keeping fluids down but no timing or association with breakfast. This is new detail not in gold.
Gen: 'no blood in the stool or urine.' Gold: 'No blood in stool'; urine blood status not mentioned. Absence of urinary blood is an added element.

Gen: intermittent, crampy umbilical pain. Gold: periumbilical cramps that come in waves, worse when needs to open bowels. While conceptually similar in location/character, 'intermittent' vs 'comes in waves' and absence of trigger makes this a rephrased and incomplete representation; not directly supported verbatim, so considered an addition/modification.

Gen: normal bowel habit prior to illness (unspecified). Gold: normal habit once per day. Loss of quantitative detail makes this a generalized summary; it's loosely consistent but not exactly supported. Classified as addition because it omits specific daily frequency.

Gen: 'vitamin D daily.' Gold: 'Vitamins' without specifying type or regimen. Asserting vitamin D daily adds a specific agent and schedule that are not documented, which conflicts with the nonspecific gold entry.
Naproxen PRN for cramps is not mentioned anywhere in gold. Introducing a specific NSAID use contradicts the gold drug history, which lists only vitamins.
Gen: no allergies documented. Gold contains no allergy information at all. This is a new statement not supported or contradicted by gold.

Gen: drinks alcohol socially. Gold: ~1 pint a week. 'Socially' lacks the quantitative detail and does not reflect the specific weekly amount; this is a vague reformulation rather than a supported restatement.

Gen: 'not sexually active.' Gold: 'No regular SI' implies sexual intercourse is not regular, but does not rule out sexual activity entirely. Saying 'not sexually active' is a stronger, conflicting statement.

Gen: vitals not documented. Gold note section provided has no physical exam or vitals; however, absence in this excerpt does not prove not documented in the original source. This is an inference not supported by gold.
Similarly, claiming physical exam findings are not documented is an inference beyond the provided gold content.

Gen consolidates urine timing (supported by hpi-010) with 'no blood in urine' (not in gold) and 'color not observed' (present in gold). The 'no blood in urine' part is additional; overall this mixed statement includes unsupported elements, so treated as addition.

Gen states that abdominal pain location and character are based only on patient report with no objective exam. Gold provides only HPI descriptors and no exam; but inferring absence of exam is beyond gold. Thus it is additional commentary.

Gen: 'No stool culture or laboratory tests have been discussed yet.' Gold plan-001 explicitly discusses sending stool culture if fever ongoing. Therefore, saying none have been discussed contradicts gold.

Gen: acute infectious gastroenteritis likely viral; possible bacterial etiology. Gold: gastroenteritis ?viral/?food poisoning (viral vs food-related). Gen removes 'food poisoning' and introduces 'possible bacterial' etiology, altering the differential. This conflicts with the documented impression.

Gen: no objective dehydration signs documented yet. Gold does not present any physical exam or comment on objective signs of dehydration, so this is an interpretive inference, not supported explicitly.

Gen: still able to urinate but requires monitoring of hydration. Gold supports still passing urine (hpi-010) and that an urgent appointment will assess hydration (fu-001). The explicit assessment 'requires monitoring' is a clinical inference; partially grounded but not stated. Classed as addition.

Gen: urgent clinic appointment for hydration assessment AND stool sample. Gold fu-001: urgent appointment to assess hydration only. Gold plan-001: stool culture only if ongoing fever. Attaching stool sampling as part of the arranged urgent appointment contradicts gold’s conditional approach to stool culture/testing.
Gen: sample to be sent today if possible; lab faster in clinic vs post. Gold only says 'stool culture sent' if ongoing fever; no logistics about same-day sending or clinic vs post speed.
Gen: postal sample if not sent from clinic. No such postal alternative is described in gold.

Gen: consider stool culture if symptoms persist/worsen. Gold: needs stool culture if fever ongoing. Criteria differ (fever vs general persistence/worsening), so this is a modified and expanded condition rather than supported by gold.

Gen: safety-net for worsening symptoms with specific red flags (dizziness, confusion, etc.) and direct urgent care. Gold: if worse, abdominal pain, unwell, contact clinic to arrange urgent A&E. Overlaps conceptually but with different triggers and pathway; it goes beyond what gold states.
Gen: patient to call support line to book urgent appointment and clinic may expedite. Gold already has the appointment booked; there is no mention of support line booking or expediting.
Gen: extensive education about monitoring urine output and food progression. Gold has limited advice on ORT and dietary avoidance, not the broader educational detail.
Gen: advised to return if red flags or no improvement. Gold provides a narrower instruction (worse, abdominal pain, unwell) with A&E arrangement; 'no improvement' and generic red flags are extra.

Gen fu-001 repeats plan-003: urgent appointment for hydration assessment AND stool sample. Gold fu-001: urgent appointment to assess hydration status only; no stool sample tied to that appointment. This adds an unconditioned stool sample component, conflicting with gold.
